item.title: Seven & i Abandons Investment Talks with Poland’s Zabka
item.description: Japan’s Seven & i Holdings Co. has ended talks over a potential investment in Poland’s largest convenience store operator Zabka Group SA, even as it continues to look for expansion opportunities beyond its home market.

item.title: El Niño Worsens Plight of Asia’s Rice Belt After War Price Shock
item.description: A dry spell is sweeping across Asia’s rice fields, dealing another blow to farmers grappling with steep fuel and fertilizer prices triggered by the war in Iran.

item.title: Big Asia Stock Funds Turn to Laggards to Cut Risk From AI Swings
item.description: Investors in Asia are snapping up stocks from Indonesian banks to Chinese e-commerce titans and Indian technology firms, trimming bets on popular AI trades which have turned increasingly volatile.

item.title: One Paycheck No Longer Enough for Young Singaporeans in AI Age
item.description: By day, Adele Lee juggles schedules and administrative work as a personal assistant to a senior director at a financial advisory firm. Three evenings a week, the 32-year-old logs back on, this time to sell second-hand clothes through TikTok livestreams, fielding questions from viewers and packing orders herself after the broadcast ends.

item.title: Nvidia to Invest $1 Billion in Naver and Expand SK Group Accord
item.description: Nvidia Corp. will invest $1 billion in Naver Corp. to help finance an AI data center under construction in South Korea, adding to a frenzy of deals by the world’s most valuable company.

item.title: SpaceX Starship Deploys Starlink Craft During Post-IPO Test
item.description: SpaceX’s Starship deployed upgraded Starlink satellites and returned to Earth largely unscathed, advancing Elon Musk’s IPO-fueled plans to scale his dominant rocket business into an artificial intelligence and satellite communications empire.

item.title: NYC’s Initial Pied-à-Terre Tax Roll Far Exceeds Early Estimates
item.description: More than 31,000 properties are potentially subject to New York City’s new pied-à-terre tax on second homes, according to data published Friday by the city’s Finance Department.

item.title: Vitol Paid Out $5.9 Billion to Traders as Profit Halved in 2025
item.description: Commodity trading giant Vitol Group paid out $5.9 billion to its executives and senior staff through share buybacks last year, even as its profits more than halved to $4.2 billion.

item.title: CFTC Warns Prediction Markets Over Blanket Self-Certifications
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is tapping the brakes on prediction markets’ practice of “self-certifying” boilerplate contracts that could apply to myriad events.

item.title: Oil Prices Volatile as Supply Disruptions Hit Four Global Fronts
item.description: Brent futures surged past $100 a barrel as the conflict in the Middle East widens and Ukraine strikes Russian infrastructure.

item.title: Wall Street Bulls Are Staring Down $100 Oil, Tariffs, AI Angst
item.description: Every bull market has a recurring cast of villains. Oil shocks. Inflation. Rising bond yields. Trade wars. This week, investors had to contend with all of them at once.

item.title: US Cattle Herd Grows Slightly in Potential Sign of Rebuilding
item.description: The US cattle herd grew modestly from the prior year, in a signal that ranchers may be starting to retain more animals following a historic shortage.

item.title: Hedge Funds Turn Most Negative on Canadian Dollar Since 2024
item.description: Hedge funds have accumulated the most negative bets on the Canadian dollar in two years as the threat of American tariffs drags on the currency.

item.title: Fitch Upgrades Jane Street to High Grade, Citing Income Growth
item.description: Fitch Ratings upgraded Jane Street Group to investment-grade status on Friday, citing the market maker’s strong income growth throughout the economic cycle.

item.title: Oil to End Year Near $100 on Mideast Disruptions, Rapidan Says
item.description: The breakdown of the US-Iran ceasefire threatens to leave Brent crude hovering around the $100-a-barrel mark well past July and into the end of the year, according to Rapidan Energy Group’s increased forecast.

item.title: LSEG Reviews US Investment Grade Fund Flow Data After JPMorgan Flags Error
item.description: LSEG Lipper is reviewing weekly data showing US investment grade funds saw the biggest outflows in more than six years after a report published by JPMorgan Chase & Co. said there was a potential error in Lipper’s data.

item.title: Getting Ditched by Amazon Revitalized One Game Studio
item.description: Maverick Games, the maker of ‘Clutch,’ was ditched by Amazon but is doing just fine

item.title: SpaceX at $100 Would Imply Zero AI Value, Morgan Stanley Says
item.description: The selloff in SpaceX shares has driven the stock near a level that would imply investors are assigning no value to its artificial intelligence business, according to analysts at Morgan Stanley.

item.title: Colombia’s New Government Wins Historic $9 Billion CAF Offer
item.description: The Latin American development bank CAF plans to provide President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella’s administration with an unprecedented $9 billion in financing over the next four years, easing pressure on the nation’s strained public finances.

item.title: Anthropic Unveils More Cost-Efficient Model for Everyday Tasks
item.description: Anthropic PBC is rolling out a new artificial intelligence model that is meant to handle workplace tasks adeptly and affordably, a key selling point as some customers grow more cost conscious and competition increases in China.

item.title: Yen’s Slide Bolsters Appeal of Hawkish Bank of Japan Hedges
item.description: With the yen plunging to a four-decade low, a growing number of banks are advising traders to prepare for a hawkish Bank of Japan.

item.title: PE Founder, Ex-GOP Candidate Pleads Guilty to $50 Million Fraud
item.description: A private equity firm founder and onetime Republican candidate for governor of New Hampshire pleaded guilty to defrauding investors out of more than $50 million.

item.title: Google Ordered to Defend Robby Starbuck’s AI Defamation Suit
item.description: Alphabet Inc.'s Google LLC lost its bid Friday to escape a court case dangling the specter of legal liability for false statements made by an artificial intelligence chatbot.

item.title: ECB’s Lane Sets Up September as Next Key Moment for Rates
item.description: The European Central Bank will review — and potentially adjust — its policy stance in September, according to Chief Economist Philip Lane.

item.title: Russia’s Top Black Sea Oil Port Halts Loadings Amid Safety Fears
item.description: The largest Russian oil port in the Black Sea paused tanker loadings over the past several days, amid a surge in Ukrainian drone attacks in the area.

item.title: Qualcomm Plans to Increase Its Prices by Double Digits
item.description: Qualcomm Inc., the biggest maker of smartphone processors, plans to increase prices by a percentage in the double digits, a move that’s likely to ripple through much of the tech industry.

item.title: The Real Reason Behind the Private Credit-Insurance Nexus
item.description: Private gains and public losses.

item.title: Euro-Zone Resilience and More Inflation Seen in First Data for ECB
item.description: The euro zone’s initial data batch for officials mulling another interest-rate hike is forecast to show resilient expansion and faster inflation.

item.title: PE-Backed Robotics Firm Brooks Automation Said to Weigh IPO
item.description: Brooks Automation, a robotics and software automation company backed by Thomas H. Lee Partners, is considering an initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Trump’s Saudi Deal Spurs Watchdog Interest in Nuclear Settlement
item.description: Donald Trump’s plans for a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia are bringing tensions between US and South Korean reactor developers to the fore, surfacing details of a clash over market access that has garnered interest from regulators.
